scope: 131 print-only identities; prospective tabletop probes, not measured observations
goal: For each focus card, demonstrate a real choice, payoff net of Command and Actions, and legal counterplay. A failed probe is a reason to consider replacement, not automated proof of uselessness.

focus.opportunity: An Archer is in Rear; the opposing Frontline Guard is not a legal basic Archer Attack target and needs to be Shaken to open a Raider Incursion.
focus.comparison: Compare paying 2C plus an Action to Shake any opposing rank with a free basic Archer Attack that can target Rear only and be screened.
focus.failure_signal: If any-rank Shaken is always better than other 2C Tactics without a distinct setup, restrict or reprice it.

focus.opportunity: An opposing King/Captain Force is active with another opposing formation in the same Front; one is named.
focus.comparison: Compare its Shaken and −1 splash to They Let Them Through's single-formation ACTION/Name shutdown at the same 1C.
focus.failure_signal: If the new effect still never wins a different trade from They Let Them Through, redesign it.

focus.opportunity: A Scout or Ship observes a newly set enemy Stratagem in the same or an adjacent Front.
focus.comparison: Compare a +2 Strength reaction with playing an immediate 1C support card this Battle.
focus.failure_signal: If no Stratagem appears or the +2 cannot affect a contested Front, the Narrative is unplayable value.

focus.opportunity: A friendly Force completes a Named Formation with Brannoc while the enemy's Shaken Bonded formation carries a valuable Name or Bond.
focus.comparison: Compare Brannoc's 2C +1 Strength and one-time attached-card removal with a 1C Name and an independent 1C Tactic or a 1C Seized the Standard Bond.
focus.failure_signal: If the Shaken enemy never offers an attachment at completion or it produces unanswerable permanent snowball, narrow or soften the benefit.

focus.opportunity: A Captain/Scout and attached Bond share a Front before a crucial draw.
focus.comparison: Compare 1C zero-Strength Bond's filter with a normal +1-Strength Bond.
focus.failure_signal: If filtering never produces a better card or choice before resolution, a zero-Strength Bond may be too expensive.

focus.opportunity: An attached Name's continuous or ACTION effect would be suppressed by a legal opposing Tactic.
focus.comparison: Compare protection of Name text with a +Strength Bond and simply replaying the effect next Battle.
focus.failure_signal: If the opponent lacks suppression, the Bond's 1 Strength is its entire floor.

focus.opportunity: A Force becomes Named with Elian and can move into a location that creates a Rider Attack or flank.
focus.comparison: Compare free completion Move with spending a separate Maneuver ACTION and 1C.
focus.failure_signal: If the same position could be used by choosing deployment earlier, count only the real saved Action.

focus.opportunity: The top three deck cards vary sharply in usefulness over the next turns.
focus.comparison: Compare 1C Name +1 Strength with reordered draws versus an immediate card-filtering Name.
focus.failure_signal: If no follow-up draw timing matters, the ordering ability contributes little.

focus.opportunity: A Bond completes a Formation in a contested Front and its +1 this Battle would flip the Front.
focus.comparison: Compare 1C Bond's permanent Strength plus temporary bonus against other 1C Bonds.
focus.failure_signal: If the one-turn bonus does not alter result, it still enables Named; record that separately.

focus.opportunity: Choose Neris as Force or Name when a friendly formation needs a Move to open a flank or protect a support rank.
focus.comparison: Compare role cost and later ACTION against one ordinary Maneuver or Order.
focus.failure_signal: If one mode always dominates the other, log the exact alternatives.

focus.opportunity: Two adjacent active Fronts each have movable Formations with all rank placements legal.
focus.comparison: Compare one Action/3C front-column exchange and +2 to individual Moves across several turns.
focus.failure_signal: If a legal beneficial exchange cannot be staged, the card is effectively dormant.

focus.opportunity: A Shaken/Exhausted named Rider needs row movement and can still Maneuver due to Sela.
focus.comparison: Compare two movement permissions with free deployment and normal Maneuver restrictions.
focus.failure_signal: If rank change is never worthwhile, investigate narrow movement rather than price.

focus.opportunity: A Raider or Skirmisher formation in an active Front needs a Move to open an Incursion after an opponent in that Front was Shaken.
focus.comparison: Compare the 1C zero-Strength Bond and one free Move with the 1C Marched With Strength Bond and a separate 1C Maneuver.
focus.failure_signal: If the Shaken condition almost never overlaps a legal useful Move, replace the zero-Strength Bond's payoff.

focus.opportunity: A prepared Name is in the same Front as an unNamed Force and this Bond can complete it.
focus.comparison: Compare 0-Strength Bond + immediate attachment with a normal +1 Bond and an ordinary Name play.
focus.failure_signal: If it requires more setup than saved Actions, it is redundant.

focus.opportunity: A prepared Name/Bond can attach to the Force directly ahead as this Bond is played.
focus.comparison: Compare extra prep Action and 0-Strength Bond with ordinary direct attachment.
focus.failure_signal: If the preparation shortcut does not save time or grant a Named completion, flag.

focus.opportunity: A Bonded Middle formation can tax enemy Tactics targeting a valuable friendly Rear unit.
focus.comparison: Compare 0-Strength defensive Bond with a +1-Strength Bond and a Guard screen.
focus.failure_signal: If tax has no practical deterrent, identify better trigger.

focus.opportunity: A 3-Strength Aradai is played into Frontline opposite a 3-Strength defender with an opposing Rear target; its temporary -1 permits an immediate later Raider Incursion.
focus.comparison: Compare Aradai's 3C baseline body and one-Battle defender -1 with Thirty Spears at 2C (no Attack) and a stronger 4C Raider.
focus.failure_signal: If the local -1 seldom opens a legal Raider Attack before Shaken clears, its odd-Strength compensation is too situational.

focus.opportunity: A Named Middle Banner Singers faces an opponent holding a Tactic that targets another friendly formation here.
focus.comparison: Compare 3C/three-layer setup with the same turn spent adding a higher Strength Force.
focus.failure_signal: If +1 hostile cost never prevents or changes a Tactic choice, the effect is decoration.

focus.opportunity: A Rider moves after plan is set; the extra step permits a new flank or avoids a counterattack.
focus.comparison: Compare plan set +1C with two ordinary Maneuvers and with no plan.
focus.failure_signal: If the extra step is illegal or redundant, record failure.

focus.opportunity: An opposing Shaken Named formation holds a valuable Bond or Name and The Black Pursuers can spend one Action and 1 Command to return it.
focus.comparison: Compare its 1 Command ACTION after an Archer/Skirmisher Shake with another Attack, or using a hostile Tactic instead.
focus.failure_signal: If a legal attached target rarely remains Shaken or the bounce has no tactical payoff, the extra Action is unattractive.

focus.opportunity: In Battle II, another friendly Raider can be advanced by The Damar to Frontline, gaining its first legal target for a basic Raider Attack in one paid Action.
focus.comparison: Compare 4C Damar plus one free newly legal Attack with deploying a 3C line Force and then separately spending Actions to Move and Attack.
focus.failure_signal: If the extra Command premium is paid but the free Attack is almost never legally created, coordinated advance is overpriced.

focus.opportunity: A Bonded but Unnamed Rider/Skirmisher has an adjacent Front with a legal better position.
focus.comparison: Compare one-Command Maneuver to completing a Name before moving.
focus.failure_signal: If the Bond-only permission does not save an Action or Command, flag.

focus.opportunity: During Battle II, a Bonded Force in an active Front is missing a Name and you hold The Field Train plus that Name; playing Field Train in Middle is legal.
focus.comparison: Compare Field Train's 3C/2-Strength body and a no-extra-Action Name play (full Name Command paid, Guarded on completion) against spending one Action on each card or playing a stronger Force.
focus.failure_signal: If spending 3C for the weak Field Train body and saved Action never changes the Front or next-turn options, its hand deployment still fails the tempo test.

focus.opportunity: During Battle I, one Human already holds Middle and The Fifty Men are played into Frontline, activating their temporary one-Battle +1 Strength reward.
focus.comparison: Compare the 4C/5-Strength conditional temporary bonus against a 4C/4-Strength Guard with screening or the 2C Thirty Spears simple body.
focus.failure_signal: If conditional +1 makes The Fifty Men dominate other 4C roles every Battle, compensation overshoots the odd-Strength rounding margin.

focus.opportunity: An active outer Front has a Guard, Archer or Stronghold and faces a close result.
focus.comparison: Compare +2 for a 1C hidden-plan Action against regular Strength with no outer-Front gate.
focus.failure_signal: If outer Front cannot matter by activation timing, adjust deck and timing.

focus.opportunity: An Unnamed or Exhausted Grey Rider Maneuvers across an active Front boundary, causing an opposing Frontline to become flanked and eligible for its basic Rider Attack.
focus.comparison: Compare Grey Riders' single paid Maneuver plus unused Rider Attack with an ordinary Named Rider's two separate Actions and permanent Strength deployment.
focus.failure_signal: If new legal Rider targets rarely appear, the expensive combined tempo does not earn its 4C printed price.

focus.opportunity: At resolution, only your side has Named Formation and your Front is tied or losing by exactly 1.
focus.comparison: Compare its 1C resolution swing to saving the hidden-plan action for a Force/Name earlier.
focus.failure_signal: If only late rare board states work, treat as a specialist rather than automatic keeper.

focus.opportunity: Two prepared components can be attached to Forces in the same Front, one of which becomes Named.
focus.comparison: Compare the cost and Actions of preparing, playing House of Reed and using its attachment ACTION with straightforward attachment to that same Force.
focus.failure_signal: If extra Actions and 4C cannot produce earlier or stronger Named completion, flag.

focus.opportunity: You have an exposed high-value Frontline Force and an empty Middle. Play Ilyri in Middle, then swap the friendly Forces and Guard the displaced Force.
focus.comparison: Compare to putting Ilyri in Frontline normally and to spending 3C on a 3-Strength Force.
focus.failure_signal: If swap never changes a result or protection, the 2-Strength premium has no payoff.

focus.opportunity: An opponent sets a face-down plan in the same Front while Scouts are in Middle or Rear.
focus.comparison: Compare peek plus filter with a planned Attack or unconditional card selection, counting when a useful decision follows.
focus.failure_signal: If no new decision is enabled after reading the plan, the reaction is ineffective.

focus.opportunity: A Bonded Late Banner can attach a 2–4C Name, and there is still a contested Front to decide.
focus.comparison: Compare total Command/Actions saved against a 3-Strength baseline Captain.
focus.failure_signal: If discount affects no Name before Battle closes, record setup failure.

focus.opportunity: Your Skirmisher can move an opposing Frontline/Middle Force into a legal Rear slot.
focus.comparison: Compare 0C Tactic Action with They Had Gone Too Far's 1C fallback Shaken.
focus.failure_signal: If Rear is always full, the 0C card may be dead despite free Command.

focus.opportunity: A Frontline is empty, a legal Middle formation exists, and +2 turns a close final result.
focus.comparison: Compare hidden plan 1C/Action to playing an immediate Frontline Force ahead of resolution.
focus.failure_signal: If the plan routinely accomplishes no more than one extra Force, inspect flexibility.

focus.opportunity: At least two Riders have legal winning Maneuvers before resolution.
focus.comparison: Compare 2C Narrative plus moves/Actions with ordinary 1C Maneuvers and permanent strengthening.
focus.failure_signal: If players never Maneuver after playing it, static +Strength alone may not justify.

focus.opportunity: A threatened Rear Force needs Archer screening but friendly Middle Guard is Shaken.
focus.comparison: Compare the unconditional Middle screening exception with an ordinary Middle Guard.
focus.failure_signal: If Shaken screening rarely matters, note it as niche defensive rather than useless.

focus.opportunity: An opposing Tactic can target your Frontline Red Shields while both players have Command choices.
focus.comparison: Compare the 1C Tactic tax against a normal 4C Guard body's Strength and screening.
focus.failure_signal: If opponent simply chooses other targets without cost, this may still be useful; record diversion.

focus.opportunity: In Battle II, a friendly Force in the same active Front has Exhausted and Shaken; play Middle Relief Column to remove all its negative markers and give it Guarded.
focus.comparison: Compare the 3C/3-Strength body plus immediate healing and Guarded with a separate 1C Guarded Bond, White Hands' later healing ACTION, and a normal 3C Force.
focus.failure_signal: If a legal, threatened Force rarely needs recovery and Guarded before the Battle closes, its 3-Strength baseline may be doing all the work.

focus.opportunity: A River Raider occupies Frontline, outmatches an opposing Frontline after a Shake, and can use its 1C ACTION against an attached Middle or Rear Force.
focus.comparison: Compare 4C River Raider plus 1C/action for attachment pressure with Seven Black Ships immediate PLAY attachment return using the same basic Raider legal-target check.
focus.failure_signal: If extra repeat opportunities never occur before this Raider uses its Attack, Seven Black Ships dominates its sabotage role.

focus.opportunity: An opposing hidden plan in or adjacent to your Scout's Front is strategically relevant.
focus.comparison: Compare paying 1C + a Tactic Action to force a reveal/re-set choice against playing direct Strength.
focus.failure_signal: If opponent always pays 1C and no decision changes, estimate whether tax pays.

focus.opportunity: Both players contest a Front with Scout/Seer and opponent sets a hidden Stratagem there.
focus.comparison: Compare 1C + hidden-plan ACTION for Guarded versus a standalone Guarded Bond.
focus.failure_signal: If Guarded is too late or never prevents an affliction, lower priority or redesign.

focus.opportunity: Your Frontline Serekh directly protects a Middle formation from hostile Tactics.
focus.comparison: Compare 3C/3 Strength shield with just adding a stronger Frontline Guard.
focus.failure_signal: If the tax never influences targeting, assess whether its Guard class is enough.

focus.opportunity: During Battle II, an existing friendly Frontline Force can be moved one adjacent legal position by a new Middle Signal Company, changing a flank and allowing a card draw.
focus.comparison: Compare 3C/2-Strength Signal Company's immediate free-Action Move and optional draw against a 3C/3-Strength Damar's same-Front forward Move and a 1C ordinary Maneuver.
focus.failure_signal: If the extra movement reach and possible flank draw never compensate for one less Strength versus Damar, this remains a poor deployment choice.

focus.opportunity: A Vardai can legally Move an adjacent empty position and then make a newly positioned basic Rider Attack; its once-per-Battle ACTION is unused.
focus.comparison: Compare its 1C once-per-Battle Move plus unused Rider Attack within one Action against a Named Rider Maneuver followed by a second Attack Action.
focus.failure_signal: If the resulting target is almost never legal, its once-per-Battle move remains an expensive Action-only reposition.

focus.opportunity: An opponent has a relevant hidden plan before your scouting ACTION; you can change the next card played based on the reveal.
focus.comparison: Compare extra ACTION spent inspecting/filtering with playing your best available card immediately.
focus.failure_signal: If the peek never changes a next action, the information is too passive.

focus.opportunity: A Force directly ahead is Shaken before Front resolution and the Middle/Rear Healer can clear it.
focus.comparison: Compare spending an ACTION to remove the condition versus playing a +Strength card and retaining tempo.
focus.failure_signal: If its healing ACTION is repeatedly weaker, the 3-Strength body alone may not justify it.

focus.opportunity: A Seer supports Named formations in current or adjacent Front and one moved Force can contest a Front.
focus.comparison: Compare temporary +1 plus movement and conditional multi-Front Strength to a 1C Bond or another Narrative.
focus.failure_signal: If Seer synergy never activates, assess the standalone PLAY ability.

focus.opportunity: An opposing Named ACTION formation could activate in a contested Front.
focus.comparison: Compare the 1C suppression + Name Strength loss against All Banners Forward's Shaken/second target.
focus.failure_signal: If target has no usable ACTION and no Name, record whether another Tactic was clearly better.

focus.opportunity: During Battle I, a friendly formation already occupies Frontline; play Thirty Spears into Middle to grant that formation +1 temporary Strength.
focus.comparison: Compare Thirty Spears at full 3C and its small +1 supporting PLAY with 3C Aradai's Frontline entry penalty and 4C Fifty Men body.
focus.failure_signal: If the support point never changes a Front or makes the 3C vanilla-style body worse than other 3C choices, revisit its role.

focus.opportunity: Tovan is attached as a Name early enough to discount multiple later Bonds and Names.
focus.comparison: Count actual Command saved and extra Actions vs 4C Name cost, and compare playing as 3C Force.
focus.failure_signal: If discount cannot repay its cost before Command recovery declines, price again.

focus.opportunity: One poor card in hand can be scheduled behind a high-value topdeck in a future draw sequence.
focus.comparison: Compare 1C Bond with normal discard-two-to-draw-one and Sorin's filtering.
focus.failure_signal: If topdeck cycling never changes decisions, count only its Named-enabling role.
